# Temple Scroll Column 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 37 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**37:1** The city that I shall sanctify, establishing My name and My temple within it, shall be holy and clean.

**37:2** Nothing impure shall exist within it; everything in it shall be clean.

**37:3** Everything that enters it shall be clean, and everything that leaves it shall be clean.

**37:4** All wine brought into it shall be clean; all oil brought into it shall be clean.

**37:5** All food brought into it shall be clean; no impure food shall be introduced into it.

**37:6** The skins of animals slaughtered within the city shall be clean, and they may be used for any sacred purpose.

**37:7** You shall not bring into My city the skin of any animal slaughtered outside it — even if it is otherwise clean — for it was not slaughtered within My temple city.

**37:8** You shall not defile My city with the skin of any animal that was not slaughtered in My presence.

**37:9** As the city is holy, so also must everything within it be holy; as the temple is holy, so must the city that surrounds it be holy.

**37:10** You shall not introduce into the city any impure creature — neither impure beast nor impure bird.

**37:11** All wine, oil, and food that enters the city shall be clean.

**37:12** You shall not bring the skin of any impure animal into it, nor shall you work with such materials within the city.

**37:13** For the city is holy to the LORD your God; I have placed My name upon it and My temple in its midst.

**37:14** It shall remain holy, clean, and pure before Me for all generations.

**37:15** Nothing abominable shall be found within it, for it is the dwelling place of My name.

**37:16** I, the LORD, am its God, and I shall dwell in it forever.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 37 extends the holiness of the temple to encompass the entire temple city. The unique skin regulations restrict the use of animal hides to those from locally slaughtered animals. The concentric holiness concept (temple > city > land) is a distinctive feature of the Temple Scroll theology.*
